stimulus.text:
United States military occupations in Latin America came to an end in the 1930s.

| Country | Year the last United States Marines left |
| Nicaragua | 1933 |
| Haiti | 1934 |

Paraphrase: At the Inter-American Conference in Montevideo, Uruguay, in December 1933, Secretary of State Cordell Hull signed a declaration that no nation has the right to interfere in the internal or external affairs of another nation.
stimulus.source_note: Occupation end years from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11, and Princeton Review, Chapter 11. Montevideo declaration paraphrased from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11.

source: original; table from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.11, and Princeton Review, Chapter 11; Montevideo declaration paraphrased from Barron's
stem: At Montevideo in 1933, Secretary of State Cordell Hull signed a declaration that no nation has the right to interfere in the affairs of another. That declaration mattered most because it did which of the following?

options.text: Rejected the legal claim behind decades of intervention
Gave the United States new bases in Latin America
options.misconception: The policy cut the military presence; bases were not the point.

options.text: Ended all American trade with Latin America
options.misconception: Trade grew instead, through the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934.

options.text: Brought Latin American nations into the League of Nations
options.misconception: Latin American nations were already in the League; the declaration was about non-intervention.

rationales.A: The declaration took away the claim, used since the Roosevelt Corollary, that the United States could police the hemisphere.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the Good Neighbor Policy wound down occupations instead of adding bases.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 expanded trade with Latin America.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the declaration concerned intervention, not League membership.
rationales.general:
1. Since the Roosevelt Corollary of 1904, the United States had claimed a right to intervene in Latin America.
2. Marines had occupied Nicaragua, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic under that claim.
3. At Montevideo the United States signed a rule that no nation may interfere in another's affairs.
4. That signature gave up the legal claim itself, and the Platt Amendment's repeal in 1934 followed the same logic.
Remember: a declaration matters when it takes away your own claimed right.
